name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2 million example open-source dataset for training reasoning models via supervised fine-tuning (SFT). It covers math (850,000 examples), code (250,000 examples), and science (100,000 examples) domains. The dataset is the result of a systematic investigation of over 1,000 controlled experiments across each step of a data generation pipeline, including question sourcing, mixing, filtering, deduplication, multiple answer sampling, and teacher model selection. Answers (reasoning traces) are generated using QwQ-32B as the teacher model. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on this dataset yields OpenThinker3-7B, a state-of-the-art open-data reasoning model at the 7B scale.

rai:dataCollection: The dataset is constructed through a multi-stage pipeline: (1) sourcing questions from existing datasets and newly generated synthetic datasets across math, code, and science domains; (2) mixing questions from top-performing sources; (3) filtering questions using LLM-based methods (difficulty-based or response-length-based filtering); (4) deduplicating questions and sampling multiple answers per question (16x) using QwQ-32B as the teacher model; and (5) no answer filtering (found to not improve performance). Over 1,000 controlled ablation experiments were conducted to determine the best strategy at each pipeline step. The final dataset contains 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Experiments, Web API
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions are sourced from 27 code sources (e.g., StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, KodCode-V1), 21 math sources (e.g., OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath-1.5, MathPile), and 14 science sources (e.g., StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDFs, CQADupStack-Physics). Sources include online forums (StackExchange, CodeForces, AoPS), competition datasets, LLM-generated synthetic datasets, and textbook-extracted questions. Answers (reasoning traces) are generated by querying QwQ-32B as the teacher model.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions are mixed from top-performing sources (top 1-2 sources per domain). For math and science, exact deduplication is applied using Normalized Indel similarity (LCS-based). For code, no deduplication is applied. Multiple answers (16x) are sampled per question from the teacher model (QwQ-32B). Datasets are decontaminated against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram similarity (N=13) methods, removing samples flagged by either criterion.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Question filtering: difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code (rating questions 1-10 on ICPC rubric, keeping hardest); response-length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science (annotating questions and keeping those with longest LLM-generated responses). Deduplication: exact match deduplication for math and science using Normalized Indel similarity; no deduplication for code. Decontamination: samples with >=75% Indel similarity or shared 13-grams with evaluation benchmarks are removed. No answer filtering is applied in the final pipeline.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers (reasoning traces) are generated by querying QwQ-32B as the teacher model, sampling 16 responses per question. For question filtering, GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini/nano are used to assess question difficulty or generate responses for length-based selection. For question sourcing involving synthetic generation, GPT-4o-mini is used with specific prompts to generate or extract questions from seed texts. No human annotation of answers is performed; all reasoning traces are machine-generated.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: DeepSeek API (for pipeline experiments with DeepSeek-R1), QwQ-32B (final teacher model, run on 16 1xNvidia GH200 nodes), GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini/nano (for question filtering and synthetic question generation via OpenAI API), Gemini gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (for PDF OCR in science pipeline), LlamaFactory (training framework)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Ablation experiments (1,000+) were conducted at 31,600 examples per strategy to evaluate each pipeline step. Strategies were selected based on average benchmark performance across math, code, and science domains. Answer filtering experiments showed that no filtering strategy significantly outperformed training on all samples, so answer filtering was omitted from the final pipeline. Deduplication experiments showed that exact deduplication with 16x sampling was optimal or near-optimal across domains.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts3-1.2M. The codebase is released at https://github.com/open-thoughts/open-thoughts. The project has gone through multiple generations (BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, OpenThoughts3-1.2M). No explicit deprecation policy or update schedule is stated.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and resulting models are intended to democratize access to strong reasoning AI by providing open-source alternatives to proprietary reasoning datasets. The authors note that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of base models (e.g., OpenThinker3-7B shows increased harmfulness rates on Harmbench: 55.5% vs. 14.5% for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), consistent with prior findings on fine-tuning aligned models. The authors acknowledge the challenge of balancing safety and utility in reasoning models and suggest future work should incorporate safety-specific datasets.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses exclusively on math, code, and science domains and does not cover other reasoning domains. Question sources are predominantly English. The pipeline selects from a limited number of top-performing question sources (top 1-2 per domain), which may reduce diversity. Distilled reasoning models trained on this data show generalization deficits, exhibiting strong performance fluctuations on reasoning-invariant problem variations (Alice in Wonderland evaluation), indicating they do not robustly generalize despite improved average performance.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not include data for reinforcement learning training. It does not explore staged SFT or curriculum learning. The pipeline optimizes for average benchmark performance across domains rather than per-domain optimization, which may not be optimal for individual domains. The dataset is limited to math, code, and science; other reasoning domains (e.g., legal reasoning) are not covered. Some benchmarks saturate at large scales (AMC23, MATH500) and others do not respond to scale (HLE). Training on this data degrades safety alignment of base models.
rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of language models to improve reasoning capabilities in math, code, and science domains. The dataset is used to train OpenThinker3-7B (from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) and has also been tested with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It is intended for the research community to build open reasoning models. Not recommended for reinforcement learning training pipelines without adaptation, and not recommended for safety-critical applications without additional safety alignment.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 16 answers (reasoning traces) are generated per question from the teacher model (QwQ-32B) in the final pipeline.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (teacher model for answer/reasoning trace generation), DeepSeek-R1 (teacher model used in pipeline experiments and earlier dataset versions), GPT-4o-mini (question difficulty filtering, response-length filtering, synthetic question generation, majority consensus verification, GPT verification, English verification, long paragraph verification), GPT-4.1-mini (response-length filtering for math and science), GPT-4.1-nano (response-length filtering), Gemini gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (PDF OCR for organic chemistry pipeline), FastText classifiers (question and answer filtering), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (embedding-based question filtering), Evalchemy (evaluation framework)
